system.name: DNA-DetectLLM
system.one_liner: A zero-shot detector of AI-generated text that builds an ideal AI sequence for each input, repairs non-optimal tokens and scores the cumulative repair effort.

content.variant_note: a DNA analogy of template and replicated token strands linked by Repair and Mutate arrows, beside two stacked cards contrasting overlapping and separated score histograms
content.argues: Scoring the repair effort of a mutation-repair process separates machine and human text with less overlap than traditional detection scores.
content.subject: A DNA-style pair of token strands linked by Repair and Mutate arrows, beside two cards contrasting overlapping and separated score histograms.

evidence: The input sequence can be analogized to a replicating strand, while the ideal AI-generated sequence corresponds to the template strand.
constructs an ideal AI-generated sequence for each input, iteratively repairs non-optimal tokens
quantifies the cumulative repair effort as an interpretable detection signal

summary: DNA-DetectLLM is a zero-shot detector of AI-generated text. For each input it builds an ideal AI-generated sequence, repairs non-optimal tokens step by step and uses the cumulative repair effort as the detection signal. Figure 1 explains this through a DNA analogy. The left panel draws a template strand (the ideal sequence) above a replicated strand (the input) as rows of rounded token boxes x1 to xL: blue boxes with smiley badges are fine, pink boxes with angry virus badges are mutated. A large hatched blue up arrow labelled Repair and a pink down arrow labelled Mutate sit between the strands, each with a one-pair mini example. On the right, two stacked cards compare traditional paradigms (overlapping histograms, red cross) with mutation-repair (separated histograms, green check).
summary_zh: DNA-DetectLLM 是零样本 AI 生成文本检测方法。图左用 DNA 类比：模板链与复制链上的词元由“修复”和“突变”两个大箭头相连；图右两张卡片对比传统范式（直方图重叠、红叉）与突变-修复范式（分离、绿勾）。
notes: No paragraph of the paper mentions the figure, so the roles of Repair and Mutate, of the blue and pink tokens and of the badges are read off the figure, the caption and the abstract only. The extraction holds 35 bitmaps: 22 token badges, the logo, two strand icons, the check and cross, the block arrows and the large arrows; the histograms look like vector shapes.
